quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: For a driver 21 years or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 or older cannot legally drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep a steady speed through the entire curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve and gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up into a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians who have the green light.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are traveling at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
Road construction is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane on a multilane road is ending. Drivers in that lane must move left.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Require a tune-up sooner than normal.
Make you feel drowsy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from the engine. A leak lets dangerous fumes into your car. These fumes can make you drowsy while driving and are very harmful.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded by the bright lights and lets you see the road well enough to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is about to appear. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn and emergency signals when needed.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you face the traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: If a sign does not prohibit it, can a driver turn left at a red light?

options.text: Yes, onto any street if no other vehicles or pedestrians are present.
No, never.
Yes, from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
Yes, from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: You can turn left on a red light from a one-way street onto another one-way street moving to the left, unless a sign says you cannot. You must stop completely and check that no vehicles or pedestrians are in your way.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross, since trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park a car.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Do not cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
Only have a general idea of where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance. Check a map before you start driving. Do not start with just a vague idea of your destination.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Always identify yourself and help if needed. Do not leave the scene without doing this.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road.
The center of the road.
The right side of the road.
The left side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded by the headlights and lets you see the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for traffic, then go if clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When two railroad tracks are next to each other, what should you do after one train passes?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed.
You must always stop before crossing.
Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train on the other track after one train passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is approaching on either track.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a highway, turn into or out of a driveway, or make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get in a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel after your seat is in the right position.

questions.question: When there is no stop line or crosswalk at an intersection where you must stop, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in each direction, even if you must enter the intersection.
Stop where you can clearly see traffic coming before you enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see traffic coming before you enter the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest point to the intersecting road where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: When can you pass a school bus on an undivided road?

options.text: Never.
When the red lights are flashing.
When the red lights are not flashing.
Anytime if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the red lights are not flashing.
questions.explanation: Never pass a school bus from either direction when its red lights are flashing. You may pass normally when the red lights are off.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need a longer distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on surfaces with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is coming toward you.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is coming toward you.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not heading toward you.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is coming from behind you or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive in dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive in ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to drive in ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive in ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed for ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the limit, but never faster. You must drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.
